NO. 005 · Songbirds & City Birds / Motacillidae · Wagtails & Pipits

White Wagtail

白鹡鸰 · bái jí líng Motacilla alba
Winter visitor Abundant 16–19 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

The little gentleman who walks with a bob and pumps his tail

Black, white and grey, walking with the tail pumping like a metronome. In winter the White Wagtail is the easiest bird in South China to meet: car parks, riverbanks, paddy bunds, the paving outside a block of flats — it will drop in and walk about anywhere.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • HeadCrown black, face white, throat black (the South China subspecies leucopsis has a white throat and lores and an even whiter face), giving a crisp black-and-white division.
  • PlumageUpperparts grey (darker-backed in leucopsis), wings black and white, underparts white to pale grey, often with a faint grey band at the sides of the breast.
  • TailLong, black and white with white outer feathers; pumped up and down almost constantly while perched — the most reliable identification behaviour.
  • FlightA pronounced bounding flight, calling as it goes, with obvious white underwing.

Behaviour

A ground bird by preference: quick walks over open hard surfaces, a pause, another walk, picking insects as it goes. Flushes low and short. A winter visitor in South China, widespread from late September to April in cities and farmland, usually alone or in small parties, roosting communally on wires or in reeds.

Voice

Field recording

Recording Pascal Christe · Licence CC BY-SA 4.0 · Original file

A clear two-note 'chi-sick' or 'tzi-zi', the first short, the second rising; it calls constantly in flight and is one of the defining sounds of a winter riverbank.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • open ground along Lovers' Road
  • Xiangshan Lake Park trails
  • Doumen field bunds
  • car parks and plazas
Field note
Watch the movement before the colour: a small bird walking in stops and starts on the ground, tail pumping hard, is almost certainly a wagtail.
